chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:
There is no right of pre-emption for a Jew or a Christian, and there is no pre-emption except for a partner who has not yet divided.

key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيِّ: a Christian, mentioned here as excluded from this legal entitlement
key_terms.الْيَهُودِيِّ: a Jew, mentioned here as excluded from this legal entitlement
key_terms.شَرِيكٍ: a co-owner or partner in property
key_terms.شُفْعَةٌ: the right of pre-emption in shared property
key_terms.مُقَاسِمٍ: one who has divided the property; here, pre-emption applies only before division

ai.seo_question: Who is entitled to shuf'ah (pre-emption) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning shuf'ah, limiting it to an undivided partnership. It also negates this right for a Jew or a Christian in the case described here, while affirming that shuf'ah applies only where joint ownership remains undivided.
